claim: ACRP Research Report 175 recommends a minimum Speech Transmission Index (STI) of 0.45 and a signal-to-noise ratio of 10 to 15 dB(A) for airport PA in pier-style departure lounges.
source_title: Improving Intelligibility of Airport Terminal Public Address Systems — Chapter 3: Speech Intelligibility
supporting_excerpt: Codes and application standards typically recommend a minimum STI of 0.45 or 0.50. STI values range from 0 to 1, with numbers close to 1 achieving high levels of intelligibility. The study recommends maintaining an SNR of 10 dB(A) and a minimum STI of 0.45 for public address broadcasts in pier-style departure lounges.
caveat: Recommendation, not a mandatory federal requirement. Applies to pier-style lounges specifically.

claim: IEC 60268-16 Edition 5 (2020) defines the Speech Transmission Index measurement standard used to certify PA and voice-alarm intelligibility.
source_title: IEC 60268-16:2020 — Sound system equipment — Part 16: Objective rating of speech intelligibility by speech transmission index
supporting_excerpt: IEC 60268-16:2020 defines the STI model, test signals, measurement and prediction methods.
caveat: Paywalled standard; MWAA Design Manual can cite by number without republishing content.

claim: STIPA per IEC 60268-16 is the internationally recognized method for measuring speech intelligibility in voice-alarm and PA systems; a STIPA value of 0.50 or above is typically required for EN 54-16, BS 5839-8, and ISO 7240-19 compliance.
source_title: Alarm & PAGA Testing — Voice Alarm System Commissioning
supporting_excerpt: A STIPA value of 0.50 or above ('Fair') is typically required for voice alarm systems to comply with EN 54-16, BS 5839-8, and ISO 7240-19. STIPA measurement per IEC 60268-16 is mandated by EN 54-16, BS 5839-8, ISO 7240-19, and IEC 60849 for voice alarm system commissioning, acceptance testing, and annual inspection.
caveat: Vendor-authored explanation of standards; underlying standards (IEC 60268-16, EN 54-16) are the authoritative sources.

claim: London City Airport has operated a silent terminal policy since 2008 in which no routine flight or gate announcements are made and information is displayed on screens; announcements are used only for emergencies.
supporting_excerpt: No flight or gate announcements will be made, instead all information will be displayed on screens that are located throughout the lounge and restaurants. In the case of emergency are announcements made.
caveat: Operator statement of policy. Traveler demographic at LCY is heavily business/short-haul European, not comparable to IAD international-connection profile.

claim: Finavia's Silent Airport project at Helsinki-Vantaa eliminated general flight and passenger announcements in the terminal, retaining gate-area and emergency announcements, and directs passengers to departure screens, the airport website, and the mobile app.
source_title: Helsinki Vantaa to be made a quiet airport
supporting_excerpt: The airport authorities of Finavia decided to make Helsinki Vantaa a quiet airport starting in the beginning of June, which means no flight or passenger announcements will be made in the terminal. However, announcements in the gate areas as well as emergency announcements will not be affected.
caveat: Secondary trade press summarizing a Finavia announcement; primary Finavia press release not located in this search.

claim: Copenhagen Airport does not make 'Go to gate' or 'Boarding' announcements over loudspeakers; passengers are directed to the FIDS screens and the CPH mobile app.
source_title: Go to gate and boarding in Copenhagen Airport
supporting_excerpt: At Copenhagen Airport, there are no disruptive loudspeaker announcements for 'Go to gate' and 'Boarding' - all information is displayed on screens in the airport. Passengers are advised to keep an eye on their departure on the screens or in the CPH app.
caveat: Direct operator statement; scope limited to routine gate/boarding announcements.

claim: SFO's Quiet Airport program is reported to have removed more than 90 minutes of daily unnecessary announcement time and reduced onsite noise by more than 40%.
source_title: San Francisco Airport Removed 90 Minutes of Daily Noise — Travelers Say It Changed Everything
supporting_excerpt: The scheme has already helped remove over 90 minutes' worth of unnecessary daily noise throughout the airport and reduced overall onsite noise by more than 40%.
denominator: daily airport-wide announcement time; unspecified onsite noise baseline
caveat: Figures are self-reported by SFO and repeated in trade press; underlying measurement methodology was not located in publicly available primary sources.

claim: Renkus-Heinz ICONYX Gen5 beam-steerable column arrays support up to eight independently aimable steerable beams per column with software-controlled DSP and up to 170 ms of onboard delay; the product line has been installed at LAX and thousands of other venues since 2005.
supporting_excerpt: Since 2005 Renkus-Heinz has been leading the field in Digitally Steerable loudspeakers. ICONYX has been installed in thousands of projects worldwide, from LAX International Airport in Los Angeles to the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, China. Up to eight steerable beams can be individually shaped and aimed from a single column using software-controlled DSP.
units: beams per column; ms of DSP delay
caveat: Vendor marketing; airport-installation claim (LAX) is not independently audited but is widely cited in AV trade press.

claim: Holosonics Audio Spotlight produces a narrow directional sound beam using modulated ultrasonic carriers; the vendor claims 10x greater isolation than conventional loudspeakers and reports thousands of installations since 2000.
source_title: Directional Speaker Technology — Audio Spotlight by Holosonics
supporting_excerpt: The Audio Spotlight by Holosonics beams sound in a precise, narrow column — 10x more isolated than any loudspeaker. Since 2000, thousands of Audio Spotlight systems have been installed in a wide range of applications around the world.
caveat: Vendor claim; independent A/B measurement not located in this search.

claim: Gatwick Airport installed approximately 2,000 Bluetooth Low Energy beacons across both terminals to support AR-based indoor navigation, using battery-powered devices to compress deployment into approximately three weeks, as part of a £2.5 billion transformation program.
source_title: UK's Gatwick Airport installs 2,000 Bluetooth beacons for AR-based indoor navigation
supporting_excerpt: Gatwick Airport installed around 2,000 beacons throughout its two terminals, with the beacons deployed over the course of three weeks using battery powered beacons to simplify installation and reduce costs.
caveat: Beacon count and program cost are trade press summary; SFO's approximately 500-beacon deployment is referenced separately in the same trade coverage.

claim: IEC 60118-4:2014 is the international standard for audio-frequency induction-loop systems that feed hearing-aid telecoils, specifying magnetic field strength, signal-to-noise ratio, and minimum frequency response requirements for intelligibility.
source_title: IEC 60118-4:2014 — Electroacoustics — Hearing aids — Part 4: Induction loop systems for hearing aid purposes — System performance requirements
supporting_excerpt: IEC 60118-4:2014 is applicable to audio-frequency induction-loop systems producing an alternating magnetic field at audio frequencies and intended to provide an input signal for hearing aids operating with an induction pick-up coil (telecoil). The standard specifies requirements for field strength in audio-frequency induction loops that will give adequate signal-to-noise ratio without overloading the hearing aid.
caveat: Standard is paywalled; MWAA specifications can require compliance by reference.

claim: Pittsburgh International Airport's Presley's Place is a 1,500 sq ft dedicated sensory suite that opened in July 2019 with private relaxation pods, a tactile water wall, individual and family rooms, and a simulated cabin with jetway, seats, and overhead bins.
source_title: Pittsburgh International Airport unveils Presley's Place, the world's most advanced sensory suite for special needs travelers
supporting_excerpt: Presley's Place is a 1,500-square-foot sensory suite at Pittsburgh International Airport... includes a transitional entrance, individual and family rooms, an area for adults and an 'airplane experience' complete with a cabin, seats, overhead bins and a jetway.
caveat: Facility description confirmed; capital cost not publicly disclosed in this source. 'World's most advanced' is a vendor/PR characterization.

claim: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport operates a Multi-Sensory Room inside Concourse F that includes a padded crash pit, bubble tubes, tactile panels, and soft lighting, developed with input from autism specialists.
source_title: U.S. Airports Leading the Way for Sensory-Friendly Travel
supporting_excerpt: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) introduced its Multi-Sensory Room inside Concourse F, created with input from autism specialists, featuring a padded crash pit, colorful bubble tubes, tactile panels, and soft lighting.
caveat: Trade press aggregation; ATL operator page not fetched in this search.

source_title: Airport Context Packet — MWAA (IAD and DCA), section 7
